title: My Achievements
summary: Design badges that unlock as students use the other modules.

steps.title: Add the header
steps.objective: Start the My Achievements screen with a title bar.
steps.concept: A header sits at the top of a screen and tells people where they are.
steps.expected: A title bar appears at the top of the phone.

expect.label: A Header sits in the Header zone of My Achievements
expect.fail: Drag the Header tool onto the glowing Header zone.

hints: Find the glowing Header tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the glowing Header zone of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Header, then tap the glowing Header zone.

steps.title: Name your screen
steps.objective: Give the screen a clear title.
steps.concept: The header will say “My Achievements”. A clear title means nobody gets lost.

expect.label: The header says exactly: My Achievements

hints: Click the header on the phone to select it.
Edit Text content in the Properties panel.
Type exactly: My Achievements

steps.title: Add the badge board
steps.concept: The board shows badges as locked or unlocked, with a progress bar. It reads the data the other modules saved, so it grows as students use the app.
steps.expected: A badge board appears in the Body zone.

expect.label: A Achievements sits in the Body zone of My Achievements
expect.fail: Drag the Achievements tool onto the glowing Body zone.

hints: Find the glowing Achievements tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the glowing Body zone of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Achievements, then tap the glowing Body zone.

steps.title: Design your first badge
steps.objective: Create a badge with a goal.
steps.concept: ADD BADGE needs a name, the collection to count (FOR) and the number needed (AT). Collections you can use: homework (ticked off), lessons, reminders, scores, chats, shelf and safety.

expect.label: The board has at least 1 badge

hints: ADD BADGE "name" FOR "collection" AT number.
The number is not in quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add two more badges
steps.concept: Different collections give different goals: quiz scores, books on the shelf, reminders and more.

expect.label: The board has at least 3 badges

hints: Two ADD BADGE lines, one per line.
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Final style check: every colour, border, shadow and style
steps.objective: Give your screens the same colours, shapes and shadows as the model app.
steps.concept: Colours were chosen while you built each element. Now finish the whole look: every colour, background, border, corner, shadow and text style below must match the model app you tried at the start. Items you already set show a tick.
steps.expected: Your screens look exactly like the model app.
hints: Click the element on the phone first. The style box (Choose colours, borders and corners) opens by itself.
Follow the sub-steps one by one: each says which row to use and which option to click. The red dot shows where.
Text alignment and weight are in the Properties panel (right) under “Text and layout”.

steps.title: Run and check your badges
steps.objective: See your badges and their progress bars.
steps.concept: Badges unlock as students use the other modules. Locked badges show how close you are.
steps.expected: You can see every badge with its progress.

expect.name: viewed:achievements
expect.label: You saw the badge board in the running app

subs.t: Press Run Project in the top bar
Tap a badge to see its progress

hints: Press Run Project.
Tap a badge to read its progress.
Complete tasks in other modules to unlock more.

objectives: Design badges that unlock after a number of saved items.
Read data saved by the other modules.
Show progress with locked and unlocked badges.

a: The count of saved items reaches its target
mcqs.why: The app compares a count with the badge's target number.

mcqs.q: Why show a progress bar on a locked badge?
a: It shows how close the student is

mcqs.q: Why do apps use badges and rewards?
mcqs.why: Rewards make progress visible and fun.

mcqs.q: Which three things define a badge in this app?
a: A name, a collection to count and a target number
A colour, a font and a size
A grade, a SID and a date
A header, a footer and a link
mcqs.why: The collection and target tell the app when to unlock it.

mcqs.q: Why are locked badges still visible?
a: So users know what they can aim for
mcqs.why: Seeing goals makes people want to reach them.
